screening_decisions.reason: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial evaluating a systemic immunomodulator (inosiplex) for alopecia totalis. Assesses hair regrowth (effectiveness). Meets all criteria.
Randomized placebo-controlled trial of oral pulse prednisolone (systemic corticosteroid) for extensive AA. Primary outcome is hair regrowth. RCT evaluating systemic intervention.
Randomized, controlled, investigator-blinded trial comparing two topical corticosteroid formulations for mild-to-moderate AA. Evaluates hair regrowth. RCT of topical interventions.
Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of topical minoxidil for extensive patchy AA, alopecia totalis, and universalis. Assesses hair growth clearly.
Double-blind placebo-controlled RCT evaluating 3% topical minoxidil for extensive AA. Long-term efficacy assessed. Meets criteria.
Randomized double-blind half-scalp (split-body) trial of DPCP alone or combined with minoxidil. Evaluates clinical regrowth and immunologic changes. RCT of topical interventions.
Patients randomly assigned to three different treatments (topical cyclosporine, PUVA, intravenous thymopentin). Evaluates regrowth in nonresponders. RCT of various interventions.

Not a randomized controlled trial: six patients with ALA applied to different scalp areas, but no mention of random assignment. Within-patient comparison without randomization. Does not meet RCT criteria.
Randomized trial (patients randomized to topical cyclosporin in liposomal vehicle or vehicle alone). Evaluates hair regrowth in a designated patch. Topical intervention RCT.
Double-blind placebo-controlled RCT of imipramine (systemic antidepressant) for AA. Assesses clinically significant hair regrowth. Meets criteria.
Patients randomly assigned to one of three groups: topical immunotherapy, systemic interferon, or combination. RCT evaluating both topical and systemic interventions.

Double-blind study comparing topical cyclosporin to placebo; although randomization not explicitly stated, the design implies it and double-blind placebo-controlled studies are typically randomized. Topical intervention for AA.
Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial (right-to-left comparison) of clobetasol foam for moderate to severe AA. Evaluates hair regrowth. High-quality topical intervention RCT.
Randomized controlled trial of a taper of prednisone followed by either topical minoxidil or vehicle. Evaluates both systemic and topical interventions and their combination.

Not a single RCT report; this is a narrative summary of the authors' experience with topical minoxidil, referencing one double-blind study but not presenting original trial data. Does not constitute a trial.

Prospective controlled trial comparing squaric acid dibutylester, diphencyprone, minoxidil, and placebo in 119 patients. While the word 'randomized' is absent, the description as a controlled trial with multiple active arms and placebo suggests likely randomization; conservative inclusion per gatekeeper guideline.
Not an intervention trial; cross-sectional questionnaire study assessing illness perception. Does not evaluate an intervention for AA.
Methodological/discussion article about when RCTs may not be needed; not a clinical trial of an AA intervention.
Randomized double-blind controlled trial of essential oils (topical aromatherapy) vs carrier oil for AA. Evaluates hair regrowth. Clearly meets RCT criteria.
Review/update article summarizing current knowledge on AA; not an original trial.
Retrospective population-based incidence study; no intervention evaluated.
Prognostic factor analysis among patients treated with DPCP; not a randomized trial. No comparison group randomization.
Subjects were 'divided into three groups matched for age and sex'—matching without randomization. Not an RCT.
Review article on genetics; not an intervention trial.
Methodological article on quality assessment of RCTs; not a clinical trial for AA.
